{"consolidated_memory":"LONG-TERM MEMORY: Lock Timeout Issues in storage/sql/migrations/0042_add_index.sql

The file storage/sql/migrations/0042_add_index.sql has been a recurring site of lock timeout problems on the storage side. All incidents manifest with the same signal—a lock wait that trips the statement timeout—and can be reproduced by running the migration against a loaded table. However, EACH OCCURRENCE is a separate occasion with distinct triggers, root causes, and fixes.

OCCASION 1 [2026-02-11]:
- Trigger: five percent rollout bucket
- Root cause: unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- Fix: capped the attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter
- PR #3169, branch fix/lock-timeout-1
- Outcome: 10 duplicate rows per day stopped being written

OCCASION 2 [2026-03-28]:
- Trigger: sessions that arrived through the OAuth provider
- Root cause: error swallowed by a bare except clause
- Fix: narrowed the exception handler and let the failure propagate
- PR #6341, branch fix/lock-timeout-2
- Outcome: the alert stayed quiet for 62 consecutive days

OCCASION 3 [2026-04-04]:
- Trigger: first request after a cold start
- Root cause: mutable default argument shared across calls
- Fix: made the default empty and built the value per call
- PR #6592, branch fix/lock-timeout-3
- Outcome: cold start time dropped 26 percent, to 368 ms

OCCASION 4 [2026-04-26]:
- Trigger: staging read replica under normal load
- Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR #6686, branch fix/lock-timeout-4
- Outcome: memory settled at 700 MB instead of climbing past 2 GB

OCCASION 5 [2026-05-31]:
- Trigger: jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
- Root cause: missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Fix: normalised to NFC ahead of the digest
- PR #6990, branch fix/lock-timeout-5
- Outcome: throughput rose 60 percent, to 522 requests per second

OCCASION 6 [2026-08-14]:
- Trigger: after a rolling restart of the fleet
- Root cause: off-by-one in the slice bound
- Fix: corrected the bound and added a property test around it
- PR #9090, branch fix/lock-timeout-6
- Outcome: job finished in 52 minutes instead of 1 hour

All work was performed on the storage side of the same migration file. Context from earlier lock timeout work carried forward to each subsequent occasion."}
